title: Blood clotting and blood cells; Statistical tests
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PR03a#t4 term and clue written for the game; IM10#t3 term and clue written for the game; PR03a#t3 term and clue written for the game; PR03a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: IM10#N.3, PR03a#N.3, IM10#N.5, PR03a#N.11, IM10#N.7.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Degrees of freedom
items.clue: Number of categories minus 1 in a χ² calculation.

items.label: Fibrin
items.clue: Insoluble threads forming a mesh that traps red blood cells.

items.label: Critical value
items.clue: Cut-off at p = 0.05 above which a calculated result counts as significant.

items.label: Null hypothesis
items.clue: Starting statement that there is no difference, no association or no correlation.

questions.stem: Fibrinogen circulates in the blood all the time. Why does a clot form at a cut, but not throughout the blood vessels?

options.text: Thrombin, which converts fibrinogen to fibrin, is made only where clotting factors are released.
Fibrinogen turns into fibrin only when the blood at a cut is exposed to the air.
Fibrin threads are in the blood all the time, but they tangle together only where blood flow slows at a cut.
Platelets stick together into a plug at the cut, and this plug alone is the clot, with no plasma proteins needed.

questions.explanation: The cascade starts only at the wound, so thrombin, and so fibrin, forms only there. Elsewhere fibrinogen stays soluble.

questions.stem: A student measures the lengths of 20 leaves from plants growing in the sun and 20 from plants growing in the shade. She wants to know whether mean leaf length differs between the two. Which statistical test should she use?

options.text: Chi-squared, because she is comparing two groups of plants.
Student's t-test, because she is comparing the means of two sets of continuous data.
A correlation coefficient, because she wants to know whether light is related to leaf length.
No test is needed: if the two means differ, the difference is real.

questions.explanation: Two groups, one measured variable, a difference in means: that is what the t-test is for.

questions.stem: Fibrinogen circulates in the plasma of healthy people all the time, yet clots form only where a blood vessel has been damaged. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: Fibrinogen is converted to fibrin only when it is exposed to the air at an open wound, so a clot cannot form inside a vessel that is intact.
Fibrin is already present in the plasma, but its threads only become tangled into a mesh where the flow of blood is disturbed by damage.
The cascade has so many steps that it is too slow to finish unless the blood is held still against the wall of a damaged vessel.
Thrombin, the enzyme that converts fibrinogen to fibrin, is produced by a cascade that starts only when platelets release clotting factors at a site of damage.

questions.stem: A 1999 study found that children who had slept with a light on before the age of two were more likely to become short-sighted later. Later studies found that short-sighted parents were more likely to leave a light on at night, and short sight is partly inherited. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Night-time lighting causes short sight, because the 1999 correlation was found in a large group of children.
The correlation can be explained by parents' short sight, which is linked to both variables.
The 1999 correlation must have been a mistake: the children with night lights were not really more short-sighted.
The later studies prove that light at night has no effect on the eye at all.

questions.stem: The drug warfarin blocks the use of vitamin K in the liver. The liver needs vitamin K to make prothrombin. What happens to the blood of a person taking warfarin?

options.text: It clots more slowly, because without vitamin K platelets cannot stick to form a plug.
It clots normally, because platelets alone form the clot that seals a cut.
It clots normally, because fibrin threads are already present in the plasma.
It clots more slowly, because less prothrombin means less thrombin is made.

questions.explanation: Less thrombin converts less fibrinogen to fibrin, so the mesh forms more slowly. Warfarin is used to prevent unwanted clots.
